What food is Koh Samui known for? | Samui is known for southern Thai food and seafood. Its own dish is wai khua, octopus cooked in coconut milk with shrimp paste. Also try gaeng som (southern sour curry), khua kling (dry-fried curried mince), gaeng tai pla, khanom jeen noodles with fish curry, and crab curry with betel leaves. Southern food is hotter than central Thai food.
Where are the best restaurants on Koh Samui? | For an evening out, Fisherman's Village in Bophut has the widest choice. For southern seafood, Maenam and Bang Por on the north coast have two MICHELIN-recommended restaurants and the Bib Gourmand Jun Hom, while Baan Suan Lung Khai in Taling Ngam is the other Bib Gourmand. Chaweng has the most restaurants overall.
Are there MICHELIN restaurants on Koh Samui? | Yes, but no starred ones. The MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026 lists 12 Samui restaurants: two Bib Gourmands, Baan Suan Lung Khai (Taling Ngam) and Jun Hom (Maenam), and ten Selected restaurants, including Ko Seng, Kapi Sator, Khao Horm, Saffron and Koh Thai Kitchen. Baan Suan Lung Khai requires a reservation.
Where can I eat cheaply on Samui? | Eat at the night markets: the Lamai and Nathon markets open daily, with dishes at 40–80 THB and dinner for 100–250 THB per person. Si Khao in Chaweng opens daily from 17:00 to 23:00. Local Thai restaurants away from the beach roads cost about 150–400 THB per person, and 7-Eleven is the 24-hour fallback.
Is street food safe on Koh Samui? | Generally yes. Choose busy stalls where food is cooked to order and served hot, avoid seafood that has been sitting in the sun, and drink bottled water. Factory-made tube ice with a hole in the middle is safe. If you have allergies, carry a card in Thai, because peanuts and shrimp paste are in many dishes.
Do I need to tip in restaurants on Koh Samui? | Tipping is not expected but is appreciated. Round up or leave 20–50 THB in local restaurants and 5–10 % in mid-range places if service was good. Resort and upmarket restaurants often add a 10 % service charge ("++"), in which case an extra tip is optional. Market stalls don't expect tips.
What does "++" mean on a menu in Thailand? | "++" means 10 % service charge and 7 % VAT are added to the listed price, so a 1,000++ THB dinner costs 1,177 THB. Resorts, hotels, beach clubs and upmarket restaurants use it. Local restaurants and street stalls quote net prices, with nothing added.
Where can I find vegan food on Koh Samui? | Cafés in Bophut, Lamai and Chaweng serve plant-based bowls and smoothies, and most Thai restaurants will cook tofu and vegetable dishes. Look for yellow "jay" (เจ) flags for fully plant-based stalls, often near Chinese shrines. Say "mai sai nam pla" (no fish sauce) and "mai sai kapi" (no shrimp paste), because most curry pastes contain them.
Where should I eat seafood on Koh Samui? | Head to Bang Por and Maenam on the north coast, the Bang Rak beach strip, Taling Ngam in the south-west or the Lamai Seafood Market. Seafood is sold by weight, so ask whether the price is per kilo or per 100 g and confirm the total before cooking. Whole grilled fish costs about 300–500 THB at Bang Rak.
Do restaurants on Koh Samui close in the rainy season? | Most stay open, but some smaller restaurants shorten their hours or take a break in the quiet months from September to November, and beach tables move inside on wet nights. Call ahead before driving across the island in October or November. From mid-December to February, book popular restaurants a few days ahead instead.
